source.title: Affinity and Diversity: Quantifying Mechanisms of Data Augmentation
source.authors: Raphael Gontijo-Lopes; S. Smullin; E. Cubuk; Ethan Dyer

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text contains the paper and supplementary material.
record.tranche_reason: It measures how augmentation and related training conditions affect held-out performance, a conceptual test of factors that change generalization. It does not test the listed memorization, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, or sharpness versions directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many augmentation-specific results, but the flattened figure maps do not permit assigning individual values to named transforms. Rows capture separately stated aggregate outcomes, the described Rotate(fixed, 60deg) sweep, switching results, and static-versus-dynamic comparisons. Cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study tests data augmentation mechanisms, not any of V1–V8. Held-out accuracy alone does not test these versions without their specified comparisons. Dropout and architectural relaxation appear as prior work; neither is experimentally tested here.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors argue that Affinity and Diversity jointly characterize augmentation quality, that increasing the number of distinct training examples was necessary for beneficial augmentation in their experiments, and that appropriately timed switch-off can improve performance. The necessity conclusion should retain its experimental scope.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates data augmentation and its effects on model generalization rather than random-label memorization, architecture, optimizer, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or example-removal interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Augmentation transform and probability; static versus dynamic augmentation; switch-off timing; dataset. CIFAR-10 results average 10 initializations, whereas ImageNet experiments use one initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Augmentation accuracy depends jointly on Affinity and Diversity; neither metric alone predicts performance adequately.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested image classifiers, successful augmentation balances model-dependent distribution similarity and augmentation complexity.

fits_no_version.finding: Switching augmentation off can improve final accuracy and make some otherwise harmful transforms beneficial.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An augmentation's generalization benefit depends on its training schedule as well as its transform and probability.

fits_no_version.finding: Static augmentation provides no clear accuracy gain over clean training and performs worse than corresponding stochastic dynamic augmentation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing the number of distinct training inputs is crucial to augmentation benefits in the tested CIFAR-10 setting.

record.problems: ImageNet results use one initialization and have no statistical error analysis. Many individual augmentation comparisons are presented in figures or referenced CSV files rather than described numerically in the supplied text. CIFAR-10 uses a held-out validation subset for selecting switch-off timing, so the selected schedule is tuned on validation accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: Individual transform results across 204 CIFAR-10 and 223 ImageNet augmentations, and per-transform switching values, are mapped in figures and referenced full-results CSV files; individual values were not recoverable from the supplied text. Cited outcomes from prior studies are excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization under matched architectures and recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization, local connectivity, and initialization from trained convolutional networks.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance and dependence on tuning, weight decay, or switching optimizers.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and remedies through training-recipe changes.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and jointly removing dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness versus generalization gaps and competing measures. The image transform named Sharpness is unrelated.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts apply to V1–V8. All row states are cannot_determine relative to those versions; this does not negate the reported augmentation effects. ImageNet's single initialization is an uncertainty limitation, not a separate substantive finding.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Dropout intervention and its interaction with training-set size.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.

rows.subject: WRN-28-2
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; training details in supplementary material
rows.operation_detail: Train with single-transform and composite data augmentations; report augmentation performance against clean baseline.
rows.value: Many augmentations exceeded baseline; Rotate(fixed, 45deg, 50%), Cutout(16), and combinations of FlipLR, Crop(32), and Cutout(16) had test accuracy > 2% above clean baseline
rows.uncertainty: SEM for CIFAR-10 experiments; stated to be too small to show in most figures
rows.note: The paper states these examples and their relationship to baseline, but does not give their individual accuracy values in the supplied prose.
rows.check: Valid augmentation findings, but they measure none of V1–V8. The stated gains exceed two percentage points. The prose names Crop(32), whereas the methods and augmentation labels specify Crop(4); flag this source inconsistency.

rows.subject: WRN-28-2
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; training details in supplementary material
rows.operation_detail: Vary probability of Rotate(fixed, 60deg) and measure test accuracy, Affinity, and Diversity.
rows.value: Accuracy changes non-monotonically and is maximized at intermediate values of Affinity and Diversity; exact values are figure-only
rows.note: No precise test accuracy at each probability is given in the prose.
rows.check: The nonmonotonic augmentation-probability result does not measure any listed version; partial is not a meaningful claim-relative state here.

rows.subject: WRN-28-2
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; training details in supplementary material
rows.operation_detail: Switch augmentation off partway through training and complete training with clean data; compare best switch-off result with constant augmentation.

conditions.value: best point selected from approximately 25k–75k steps, in increments of approximately 5k

rows.measure: Switch-off Lift in final test accuracy
rows.baseline: Training with the same augmentation throughout
rows.value: Switch-off Lift varies by transform; for some poor-performing augmentations it brings final test accuracy above the clean baseline
rows.uncertainty: SEM across 10 initializations; exact values are figure-only or in referenced full results
rows.note: The paper reports differing outcomes across transforms but does not state individual values in this prose.
rows.check: Augmentation scheduling does not measure any listed version. This aggregates different transforms and selected switch-off times; some strong augmentations have negative Switch-off Lift.

rows.subject: WRN-28-2
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; training details in supplementary material
rows.operation_detail: Train with FlipUD(100%) and compare constant augmentation with using it only during the first third of training.

conditions.value: augmentation used for first third of training, then switched off

rows.measure: Final test accuracy relative to clean baseline
rows.baseline: Clean baseline; constant FlipUD(100%) decreases test accuracy by almost 50% compared to it
rows.value: Using the augmentation for only the first third of training yields final test accuracy above baseline
rows.note: The text gives an explicit comparison but no exact final accuracy.
rows.check: The reported improvement after switching off vertical flips is supported, but it does not test any listed version.

rows.subject: WRN-28-2
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; training details in supplementary material
rows.operation_detail: Apply static augmentation once to the training set and compare with clean baseline and dynamic augmentation.

conditions.value: same number of unique inputs in static and clean settings

rows.value: For almost all tested augmentations, static augmentation yields lower test accuracy; crop variants showing a gain differ by less than SEM; static augmentation always performs worse than its dynamic counterpart
rows.uncertainty: CIFAR-10 SEM over 10 initializations; crop gains are less than SEM
rows.note: Aggregate statements across tested augmentations; individual transform results are shown in figures/full results.
rows.check: Static versus dynamic augmentation does not test any listed version. The comparison with dynamic augmentation excludes deterministic transforms, which are trivially equal between modes. Static crop gains over clean training are smaller than SEM.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; trained for 112.6k steps
rows.operation_detail: Train with single-transform augmentations and compare held-out performance with clean baseline.
rows.value: The paper says gains from single-transform policies are expected to be small; per-transform outcomes are presented in figures and referenced full results
rows.uncertainty: No statistics from which to analyze error; one initialization
rows.note: No aggregate numerical result for the tested augmentations is stated in the prose.
rows.check: This is an experimental setup and an expectation about gains, not an extracted result. Remove or replace with actual augmentation outcomes. The ImageNet clean baseline already includes random cropping.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
